conventions.convention: The posterior-mean proposition assumes AC, a separable real Hilbert target, a supplied finite ordered or countable complete orthonormal basis, and a supplied probability kernel. Complex targets are realified.

Posterior squared-loss minimization is over the full Hilbert action space and applies on the measurable finite-second-moment domain D2, equipped with its trace sigma-algebra. Conditional-law values on marginal-null data sets remain version choices.
Metric spaces carry Borel sigma-algebras; unrolled layer inputs use the product sigma-algebra without assuming equality with the product topology's Borel sigma-algebra.

Point rules are measurable data-to-target maps; posterior samplers are probability kernels. Exactness on a declared data domain means equality with the supplied posterior measure at every datum in that domain.

Risk uses a specified joint input-target probability law and a nonnegative product-measurable loss, with target as the first loss argument. Randomized risk integrates the action kernel at each input; infinite risk is allowed.
Fitting laws can describe paired or unpaired variables. Train and test evaluation risks require joint laws on the same input-target space; no equality or risk-transfer guarantee is assumed.
The posterior sample is drawn independently of the truth conditional on the datum; exact posterior calibration in this example means equality of its conditional law with the posterior.

load_bearing.statement: A point reconstruction rule is a Borel map g:Y→Q. Finite unrolling with Borel initialization and product-measurable updates produces such a rule. A posterior sampler is a probability kernel; score fields, learned priors, and the name “learned” alone supply no reconstruction or distributional guarantee.

For a probability law P on the product input-target space and a nonnegative product-measurable loss ℓ(t,a), R_P(g)=∫ℓ(t,g(y))P(dy,dt) and R_P(K)=∫[∫ℓ(t,a)K(y,da)]P(dy,dt). Either risk may be infinite, and no inequality between training-law and test-law risks is imposed.

Assume AC. For a probability kernel into a separable real Hilbert space with a supplied finite ordered or countable complete orthonormal basis, its coordinate mean exists measurably on the finite-second-moment domain D2. For every y∈D2 and a∈H, ∫‖h−a‖²Π_y(dh)=∫‖h−μ(y)‖²Π_y(dh)+‖a−μ(y)‖². Thus μ(y) uniquely minimizes posterior squared risk over H. When Π is an RCD of square-integrable T given Y, D2 has full data-law measure and the zero extension evaluated at Y is the unique square-integrable vector with the stated scalar conditional-expectation coordinates.

seams_checked.note: Forward maps, target classes, and data-only estimators are used consistently; learned measurability requirements add no exactness or stability guarantee.
Posterior kernels are supplied rather than inferred from an arbitrary potential; evidence and null-data version qualifications are preserved.
This is a contextual prerequisite. No contraction rate or fixed-truth posterior-version guarantee is imported into learned-estimator or risk claims.
The finite-sample open problem uses expected squared loss under Borel joint input-target laws and distinguishes statistical risk from deterministic approximation.
Finite Borel point rules and empirical joint-law risks match the suppliers. The absence of automatic convergence or train-to-test guarantees is preserved.

Exact MMSE and arbitrary denoisers remain distinguished. The Gaussian lemma proves its finite-dimensional squared-risk identity directly and explicitly avoids importing the AC-dependent Hilbert proposition.
Score fields, exact conditional scores, plug-in approximations, and algorithmic samples remain distinct; posterior exactness requires separate certification.
Benchmark definitions preserve fitting/evaluation-law distinctions, measurable point or kernel rules, and specified joint-law risk without asserting transfer.
The open formulations specify their score-error, sampling, and reconstruction-risk targets without treating sampling accuracy, point optimality, or frequentist calibration as interchangeable.
